```{r libraries, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)
library(scales)
library(readr)
```

```{r load-and-classify, include=FALSE}
# ---- Constants -------------------------------------------------------------
# Série A: 20 teams, 38 rounds -> 380 matches, 38 games per team.
# Matches with 0 goals are not in the dataset, so we set these by hand.
TOTAL_MATCHES  <- 380
GAMES_PER_TEAM <- 38

SOURCE_CAPTION <- "Data: CBF | Brasileirão Série A 2024"
COL_1ST  <- "#8DA0CB"   # first half
COL_2ND  <- "#FC8D62"   # second half / stoppage highlight
COL_GOOD <- "#66C2A5"
COL_BG   <- "#FAF9F0"

# ---- Load ------------------------------------------------------------------
# One row per goal. There is NO scoring-team column, so the analysis is done
# at the match level: a stoppage-time goal counts for BOTH teams in the match.
goal_df <- read_csv("data/seria_a_goals_by_minutes.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(Match_Date = as.Date(Match_Date))

# ---- Classify --------------------------------------------------------------
# Stoppage time: 1st half after minute 45, 2nd half after minute 90
goal_df <- goal_df %>%
  mutate(
    Period = case_when(
      Event_Half == 1 & Event_Time <= 45 ~ "1st half",
      Event_Half == 1 & Event_Time >  45 ~ "1st half stoppage",
      Event_Half == 2 & Event_Time <= 90 ~ "2nd half",
      Event_Half == 2 & Event_Time >  90 ~ "2nd half stoppage",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Is_Stoppage = Period %in% c("1st half stoppage", "2nd half stoppage")
  )

stopifnot(!any(is.na(goal_df$Period)))   # every goal must have a period
```

```{r theme, include=FALSE}
# One shared theme so every chart looks like it belongs to the same article
theme_article <- function(base_size = 13) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, color = "grey30", hjust = 0,
                                   margin = margin(b = 10)),
      plot.caption  = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey40", hjust = 1),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      axis.title    = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = COL_BG, color = NA),
      plot.background  = element_rect(fill = COL_BG, color = NA),
      plot.margin = margin(12, 16, 8, 12)
    )
}
```

```{r data-prep, include=FALSE}
# ---- Bucket per minute (regular minutes + one bar per half for stoppage) ---
minute_levels <- c(as.character(1:45), "45+", as.character(46:90), "90+")

minute_df <- goal_df %>%
  mutate(
    Minute_Bucket = case_when(
      Period == "1st half stoppage" ~ "45+",
      Period == "2nd half stoppage" ~ "90+",
      TRUE ~ as.character(Event_Time)
    ),
    Minute_Bucket = factor(Minute_Bucket, levels = minute_levels)
  ) %>%
  count(Minute_Bucket, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(Is_Stoppage = Minute_Bucket %in% c("45+", "90+"))

# ---- Minute by minute inside stoppage time ---------------------------------
stoppage_min_df <- goal_df %>%
  filter(Is_Stoppage) %>%
  mutate(
    Stoppage_Minute = if_else(Event_Half == 1, Event_Time - 45, Event_Time - 90),
    Half_Label      = if_else(Event_Half == 1, "1st half (45+)", "2nd half (90+)")
  ) %>%
  count(Half_Label, Stoppage_Minute)

# fill the gaps with 0, up to the longest stoppage observed in EACH half
stoppage_grid <- bind_rows(lapply(
  split(stoppage_min_df, stoppage_min_df$Half_Label),
  function(d) tibble(Half_Label = d$Half_Label[1],
                     Stoppage_Minute = seq_len(max(d$Stoppage_Minute)))
))

stoppage_min_df <- stoppage_grid %>%
  left_join(stoppage_min_df, by = c("Half_Label", "Stoppage_Minute")) %>%
  mutate(n = replace_na(n, 0L))

# ---- Per match, then per team ----------------------------------------------
match_df <- goal_df %>%
  group_by(Key, Match_Date, Home_Team, Away_Team) %>%
  summarise(
    total_goals       = n(),
    stoppage_goals    = sum(Is_Stoppage),
    stoppage_1st_half = sum(Period == "1st half stoppage"),
    stoppage_2nd_half = sum(Period == "2nd half stoppage"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

team_df <- match_df %>%
  pivot_longer(c(Home_Team, Away_Team), names_to = "side", values_to = "team") %>%
  group_by(team) %>%
  summarise(
    goals_in_matches      = sum(total_goals),
    stoppage_goals        = sum(stoppage_goals),
    stoppage_1st_half     = sum(stoppage_1st_half),
    stoppage_2nd_half     = sum(stoppage_2nd_half),
    matches_with_stoppage = sum(stoppage_goals > 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_matches_with_stoppage = matches_with_stoppage / GAMES_PER_TEAM,
    pct_goals_in_stoppage     = stoppage_goals / goals_in_matches,
    share_1st_half            = stoppage_1st_half / stoppage_goals,
    # rank by volume vs rank by share (ties share the best rank)
    rank_volume = min_rank(desc(stoppage_goals)),
    rank_share  = min_rank(desc(pct_goals_in_stoppage))
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(stoppage_goals))
```

```{r numbers, include=FALSE}
# ---- Numbers used in the text (inline R) -----------------------------------
n_total    <- nrow(goal_df)
n_stoppage <- sum(goal_df$Is_Stoppage)
pct_stop   <- percent(n_stoppage / n_total, accuracy = 0.1)
one_in     <- round(n_total / n_stoppage)

n_1st <- sum(goal_df$Period == "1st half stoppage")
n_2nd <- sum(goal_df$Period == "2nd half stoppage")

# Average goals in a regular-time minute (1-90)
avg_regular <- sum(!goal_df$Is_Stoppage) / 90

# Average of the first 3 stoppage minutes (both halves) vs a regular minute
avg_first3 <- stoppage_min_df %>%
  filter(Stoppage_Minute <= 3) %>%
  summarise(m = mean(n)) %>% pull(m)

peak_1st <- stoppage_min_df %>% filter(Half_Label == "1st half (45+)") %>%
  slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
peak_2nd <- stoppage_min_df %>% filter(Half_Label == "2nd half (90+)") %>%
  slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

n_deep   <- sum(stoppage_min_df$n[stoppage_min_df$Stoppage_Minute >= 7])
max_min  <- max(stoppage_min_df$Stoppage_Minute[stoppage_min_df$n > 0])

pct_matches <- percent(
  sum(match_df$stoppage_goals > 0) / TOTAL_MATCHES, accuracy = 1
)

top3        <- team_df %>% slice_max(stoppage_goals, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE)
bottom1     <- team_df %>% slice_min(stoppage_goals, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
most_1st    <- team_df %>% slice_max(share_1st_half, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
most_2nd    <- team_df %>% slice_min(share_1st_half, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

league_pct  <- n_stoppage / n_total
top_share   <- team_df %>% slice_max(pct_goals_in_stoppage, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
low_share   <- team_df %>% slice_min(pct_goals_in_stoppage, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

# Biggest climber / faller between "volume" and "share" rankings
climber <- team_df %>% mutate(d = rank_volume - rank_share) %>%
  slice_max(d, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
faller  <- team_df %>% mutate(d = rank_volume - rank_share) %>%
  slice_min(d, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

avg_per_team <- round(n_stoppage * 2 / nrow(team_df), 1)  # each goal counts for 2 teams
```

## The question

Stoppage time is where matches are often decided. Using every goal of the 2024
Campeonato Brasileiro Série A, this article looks at:

- How much of the league's scoring comes after the 45' and 90' marks?
- Which minutes of stoppage time are the most dangerous?
- Which teams lived the most late drama?

**Data:** every goal of the season, with match, half and minute (`r n_total` goals, `r TOTAL_MATCHES` matches). Compiled from the official CBF match reports (súmulas).<br>
**Limitation:** the dataset does not say *which team* scored. A stoppage-time goal
therefore counts for **both** teams in the match, so this is about late drama, not
about who benefited.

## Key takeaways

- **`r n_stoppage` of `r n_total` goals (`r pct_stop`) came in stoppage time**, roughly 1 in every `r one_in`.
- **The second half dominates:** `r n_2nd` goals in 90+ against `r n_1st` in 45+.
- **`r pct_matches` of all matches had at least one stoppage-time goal.**
- **`r top3$team[1]`, `r top3$team[2]` and `r top3$team[3]`** were involved in the most stoppage-time goals; `r bottom1$team` in the fewest.

## 1. When are goals scored?

**What to notice:** the two orange bars tower over everything else
(`r n_1st` goals in 45+ and `r n_2nd` in 90+, against about `r round(avg_regular, 1)`
goals in an average regular minute). But each orange bar folds *several* minutes
into one, this might give the impression that stoppage time has more goals. Let’s normalise the counts by minutes played.


```{r chart1}
ggplot(minute_df, aes(x = Minute_Bucket, y = n, fill = Is_Stoppage)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(
    data = filter(minute_df, Is_Stoppage),
    aes(label = n), vjust = -0.5, fontface = "bold", size = 4
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = COL_1ST, "TRUE" = COL_2ND)) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    breaks = c("1", "15", "30", "45+", "60", "75", "90+"),
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.6, 1.2))        # extra room after the last bar
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(
    title    = sprintf("1 in %d goals arrives in stoppage time", one_in),
    subtitle = "Goals per minute | orange = ALL stoppage time of each half folded into one bar",
    x = "Minute", y = "", caption = SOURCE_CAPTION
  ) +
  theme_article() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 25, b = 10, l = 10)   # right padding (points)
  )
```

## 2. Normalized view

**What to notice:** the stoppage-time effect is suggestive, not proven. The 95% range for stoppage time (2.25–3.26%) overlaps with the regular range (2.22–2.54%). The 90+ bar is the strongest signal (2.30–3.64%), but with one season of data you can’t rule out chance. The 45+ bar alone (1.68–3.19%) tells you nothing on its own.

```{r chart2}
# ---- 1. Exposure: stoppage minutes actually played (CBF match reports) ----
extra_time_df <- read.csv(
  "data/serie_a_final_scores.csv"
) %>%
  filter(year == 2024) %>%
  select(game_number, first_half_extra_time, second_half_extra_time) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.integer))

extra_min_1st <- sum(extra_time_df$first_half_extra_time,  na.rm = TRUE)
extra_min_2nd <- sum(extra_time_df$second_half_extra_time, na.rm = TRUE)

# ---- 2. Normalise: goals per 100 match-minutes ----
# Regular minute: every match plays it     -> exposure = 380 minutes
# 45+ / 90+ bar : sum of stoppage minutes  -> exposure = total minutes played
rate_df <- minute_df %>%
  mutate(
    exposure = case_when(
      Minute_Bucket == "45+" ~ as.numeric(extra_min_1st),
      Minute_Bucket == "90+" ~ as.numeric(extra_min_2nd),
      TRUE                   ~ as.numeric(TOTAL_MATCHES)
    ),
    rate = n / exposure * 100
  )

# Reference: average regular-time minute, and numbers for the text
rate_regular <- sum(filter(rate_df, !Is_Stoppage)$n) / (90 * TOTAL_MATCHES) * 100
rate_1st     <- filter(rate_df, Minute_Bucket == "45+")$rate
rate_2nd     <- filter(rate_df, Minute_Bucket == "90+")$rate

# ---- 3. Chart (same layout as item 1) ----
ggplot(rate_df, aes(x = Minute_Bucket, y = rate, fill = Is_Stoppage)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = rate_regular, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey35") +
  geom_text(
    data = filter(rate_df, Is_Stoppage),
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", rate)), vjust = -0.5, fontface = "bold", size = 4
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = "1", y = rate_regular, hjust = 0, vjust = -0.8, size = 3.3,
           color = "grey30",
           label = sprintf("avg. regular minute: %.1f", rate_regular)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = COL_1ST, "TRUE" = COL_2ND)) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    breaks = c("1", "15", "30", "45+", "60", "75", "90+"),
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.6, 1.2))        # extra room after the last bar
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(
    title    = "Chance of a goal in each minute: regular time vs stoppage time",
    subtitle = "% chance of a goal per minute played | orange = stoppage time",
    x = "Minute", y = "",
    caption = SOURCE_CAPTION
  ) +
  theme_article() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 25, b = 10, l = 10)   # right padding (points)
  )
```
```{r table2}
z <- qnorm(0.975)   # 1.96 for a 95% range

# ---- 1. Goals and minutes played for each group ----
groups <- bind_rows(
  rate_df %>% filter(!Is_Stoppage)           %>% summarise(k = sum(n), minutes = sum(exposure)) %>% mutate(group = "Regular time"),
  rate_df %>% filter(Minute_Bucket == "45+") %>% summarise(k = sum(n), minutes = sum(exposure)) %>% mutate(group = "45+"),
  rate_df %>% filter(Minute_Bucket == "90+") %>% summarise(k = sum(n), minutes = sum(exposure)) %>% mutate(group = "90+"),
  rate_df %>% filter(Is_Stoppage)            %>% summarise(k = sum(n), minutes = sum(exposure)) %>% mutate(group = "Both stoppage")
)

# ---- 2. Rate, standard error and 95% range (Poisson approximation) ----
ci_df <- groups %>%
  mutate(
    rate  = k / minutes * 100,            # goals per 100 match-minutes (= % chance per minute)
    se    = sqrt(k) / minutes * 100,
    lower = rate - z * se,
    upper = rate + z * se
  )

# ---- 3. Compare each stoppage group with regular time ----
reg <- filter(ci_df, group == "Regular time")

ci_df <- ci_df %>%
  mutate(
    diff    = rate - reg$rate,
    z_stat  = diff / sqrt(se^2 + reg$se^2),
    p_value = 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z_stat)))
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(diff, z_stat, p_value), ~ ifelse(group == "Regular time", NA, .x)))

ci_df %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```


## 3. Which teams were involved in the most stoppage-time goals?

Each stoppage-time goal is counted for **both** teams in the match. We don't know
who scored, so a team's number mixes goals it scored and goals it conceded.

**What to notice:** `r top3$team[1]` (`r top3$stoppage_goals[1]`),
`r top3$team[2]` (`r top3$stoppage_goals[2]`) and `r top3$team[3]`
(`r top3$stoppage_goals[3]`) were involved in the most stoppage-time goals;
`r bottom1$team` in the fewest (`r bottom1$stoppage_goals`). The split by half is
revealing: `r most_1st$stoppage_1st_half` of the `r most_1st$stoppage_goals`
stoppage-time goals in `r most_1st$team` matches came in first-half stoppage,
while in `r most_2nd$team` matches almost all of them
(`r most_2nd$stoppage_2nd_half` of `r most_2nd$stoppage_goals`) came in the second half.

```{r chart3}
team_order <- team_df %>% arrange(stoppage_goals, desc(team)) %>% pull(team)

team_plot_df <- team_df %>%
  mutate(team = factor(team, levels = team_order)) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(stoppage_1st_half, stoppage_2nd_half),
               names_to = "half", values_to = "goals") %>%
  mutate(half = factor(half,
                       levels = c("stoppage_1st_half", "stoppage_2nd_half"),
                       labels = c("1st half stoppage", "2nd half stoppage")))

team_totals <- team_df %>% mutate(team = factor(team, levels = team_order))

ggplot(team_plot_df, aes(x = goals, y = team, fill = half)) +
  # reverse = TRUE: 1st half on the left, 2nd half on the right (matches legend)
  geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(
    data = team_totals,
    aes(x = stoppage_goals, y = team, label = stoppage_goals),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = -0.4, size = 3.8, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("1st half stoppage" = COL_1ST,
                               "2nd half stoppage" = COL_2ND)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(
    title    = "Stoppage-time goals involving each team",
    subtitle = "Goals in the team's matches, by either side (scored or conceded, unknown) | split by half",
    x = "Stoppage-time goals in the team's matches", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = SOURCE_CAPTION
  ) +
  theme_article() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

## 4. How "late" are each team's matches?

**What to notice:** raw counts favour teams whose matches simply have more
goals. Looking at the *share* of goals that came in stoppage time changes the
picture. `r top_share$team` is on top with
`r percent(top_share$pct_goals_in_stoppage, accuracy = 0.1)` and
`r low_share$team` at the bottom with
`r percent(low_share$pct_goals_in_stoppage, accuracy = 0.1)`, against a league
average of `r percent(league_pct, accuracy = 0.1)`. `r climber$team` climbs from
#`r climber$rank_volume` in volume to #`r climber$rank_share` in share, while
`r faller$team` falls from #`r faller$rank_volume` to #`r faller$rank_share`.

> **A note on noise:** there are only `r n_stoppage` stoppage-time goals in the whole
> season, about `r avg_per_team` per team. Two or three goals can move a team
> several places, so read these rankings as a description of 2024, not as proof that
> a team is "clutch" or "fragile" late in games.

```{r chart4}
team_df %>%
  mutate(
    team  = fct_reorder(team, pct_goals_in_stoppage),
    above = pct_goals_in_stoppage > league_pct
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = pct_goals_in_stoppage, y = team)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = league_pct, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey35") +
  geom_col(aes(fill = above)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(pct_goals_in_stoppage, accuracy = 0.1)),
            hjust = 1.1, size = 3.6, color = "grey10") +
  annotate("text", x = league_pct, y = 0.1, hjust = -0.08, size = 3.3,
           color = "grey30",
           label = paste0("league avg. ", percent(league_pct, accuracy = 0.1))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = COL_GOOD, "FALSE" = "grey75"),
                    labels = c("TRUE" = "Above league average",
                               "FALSE" = "At or below average")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.04))) +
  # extra room at the bottom (1.2 units) for the "league avg." label
  scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(1.2, 0.6))) +
  labs(
    title    = "Share of goals that came in stoppage time",
    subtitle = "All goals in each team's matches",
    x = "% of goals in stoppage time", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = SOURCE_CAPTION
  ) +
  theme_article() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```
